items.title: Scope, row and probe models and API
items.action: Copy docs/plans/0004/tests/tests/lib/test_writing_docstrings_dispatch_api.py to tests/lib/test_writing_docstrings_dispatch_api.py. In plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/writing_docstrings_models.py add AGENT='harness:docstring-writer', WORK_MODEL='opus', PROBE_MODEL='haiku', PROBE_NAME='_docstring_probe.py', PROBE_RECORD='writing-docstrings/probes.txt' (relative to state_dir), PROBE_SOURCE (a module with one undocumented two-line function), FileScope (path: absolute posix str; names: List[str], empty meaning all; extra forbid; line() -> 'Scope: <path>: all' or 'Scope: <path>: a, b') and DispatchRow (model, project_root, new_docstrings: bool, scopes: List[FileScope] with min_length 1, probe: bool = False; extra forbid; text() -> 'agent=<AGENT> model=<model>', 'Project root: <root>', 'New docstrings: yes|no', one Scope line per scope, then 'Probe: yes' on a probe row). In plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/writing_docstrings_api.py add DispatchError(ValueError) carrying .problems (every defect, collected before raising); first_path(tokens, cwd) -> Optional[Path] (the first path-shaped token, '::name' stripped, resolved against cwd); resolve_scope(root, tokens, cwd) per spec D1 and plan D11 (split '::' with rsplit so a drive colon survives; tokens resolved against cwd and kept inside root; a directory becomes its git ls-files tracked .py files, recursive; names checked through report and unmatched; every file parsed; scopes keyed on the resolved path and sorted by it); plan_rows(root, scopes, *, new_docstrings, parallel); write_probes(root, scopes, record) -> List[Path] (plan D12: one probe per distinct parent folder in scope order, replacing an untracked stale probe, DispatchError for a git-tracked file of that name, each path appended to record); probe_row(root, probes) (PROBE_MODEL, new_docstrings True, probe True, one Scope per probe); clear_probes(root, record) -> List[Path] (removes each recorded path under root named PROBE_NAME and untracked, skips every other entry, deletes the record, returns the removed paths in record order; [] with no record). Paths are resolve()d and printed as_posix. Export the new names in __all__. Functions under 50 lines; Optional/Union typing; no first or second person.

items.title: docstring_dispatch.py driver and its root-separation case
items.action: Copy docs/plans/0004/tests/tests/skills/test_docstring_dispatch_command.py and docs/plans/0004/tests/tests/contract/test_root_separation.py to their repo paths. New plugins/harness/skills/writing-docstrings/commands/docstring_dispatch.py, shaped like docstring_tiers.py (sys.path insert of lib, one activate(load_config(project_root(start)))): argparse with allow_abbrev=False, parse_intermixed_args (flags may sit between paths), and an error() that raises DispatchError; options --repo, --include-new/-in, --parallel/-p, --clear-probe (store_true, no path); tokens nargs='*'. start is --repo, else the folder of first_path(tokens, cwd), else cwd (plan D13). record = cfg.path(cfg.state_dir) / PROBE_RECORD. Every run first calls clear_probes(root, record); --clear-probe alone prints 'cleared <posix path>' per removed probe and exits 0. No token and no --clear-probe is a problem. Rows print separated by one blank line; with -p and two or more rows, write_probes runs after every check passes and probe_row prints before the work rows. A DispatchError or ConfigError prints one 'problem: <text>' line per defect on stderr, exit 1, nothing on stdout and no probe written. The module docstring states the usage.

items.title: docstring-writer agent and dispatching SKILL.md through the strap gate
items.action: First mkdir -p docs/plans/strap/_archive, then git mv docs/plans/strap/writing-docstrings to docs/plans/strap/_archive/writing-docstrings-187 (D10), then run strap.py new writing-docstrings --edit (base HEAD) and continue harness:strap-skills from step 2. Before adding docstring-writer role scenarios or running check, write a frontmatter-only plugins/harness/agents/docstring-writer.md (name docstring-writer, model opus, tools Read, Edit, Grep, Bash), register it with add_part, and add 'harness:docstring-writer' to DEFINED_AGENTS in plugins/pr-review-watch/hooks/contract.ts in sorted position (after harness:bubble-memo-reviewer); the body is written at strap step 10 against the baselines. Behaviors: mechanical - SKILL.md runs docstring_dispatch.py through hpy and dispatches harness:docstring-writer; the agent file runs the tier command through hpy, reads ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/writing-docstrings/docstring_format.md, names every flag, the full-tier threshold, the D7 prompt lines, the D8 reply headings and the J4 probe reply lines (the contract-test pins move from the SKILL.md body to the agent file). Judgment - J1-J4 of plan D15; B6-B8 are not re-baselined (D15). The agent body holds the procedure now in SKILL.md (What a restyle touches, Procedure, Tier 1-3, All tiers), the New docstrings rule, the Scope-only edit rule, the probe reply and the D8 reply. SKILL.md becomes: split the arguments, interpret intent (D3 and D14; non-argument instructions of a plain request become the Developer guidance line), answer a layout question from docstring_format.md, run the driver, dispatch the probe row alone, stop on any BLOCKED or permission prompt (fix with update-config, rerun the driver), then run the driver with --clear-probe, dispatch every work row in one message with the Developer guidance line appended, relay the replies (the session may read the files to paste docstrings back when asked); it states the D5 departure from harness:parallel2 and its reason. The Use-when description stays; the argument-hint gains -in and -p.

decisions.question: How are files and symbols named on the command line?

options.summary: bare path = all; file.py::name narrows; bare symbols only with one file; directory = tracked .py files
one Symbols line for the whole row

decisions.rationale: Spec D1 after the builder check: each file carries its own scope.

decisions.question: How is the undocumented-symbols question answered?

options.summary: --include-new / -in, default off, sets New docstrings: yes|no
the agent asks the developer during the run

decisions.rationale: Developer decision; a subagent cannot pause for an answer.

decisions.question: Where does a request for new docstrings in words set -in?

options.summary: the session reads the request and the -- tail and passes -in; restyle words never do
only the literal flag sets it

decisions.rationale: Interpreting intent is the session's job (issue goal 2).

decisions.question: How does one invocation split across files?

options.summary: --parallel / -p, default off; one row per file, one row for a single file
always one agent

decisions.question: Where do parallel agents write, and where does the tool probe edit?

options.summary: direct edits in the checkout; probe file _docstring_probe.py beside the first target
direct edits; probe under state_dir
one parallel2 worktree per file

decisions.rationale: Developer decision: one file per agent is disjoint by construction; the probe meets the real Edit allow rules.

decisions.question: Which model runs a work row?

options.summary: opus in both modes
sonnet

decisions.question: What is the dispatch row format?

options.summary: agent=<type> model=<m>, then Project root, New docstrings, one Scope line per file, Probe: yes on the probe row
a JSON object per row

decisions.rationale: Same header as the pr_review, strap and bubble_memo rows.

decisions.question: What does the agent reply?

options.summary: per file: tier lines, Rewritten, Kept (in layout), Undocumented (rerun with --include-new), Defects (not fixed), Check
free text

decisions.rationale: The session relays it unedited and concatenates -p replies in row order.

decisions.question: Which tools does the agent carry?

options.summary: Read, Edit, Grep, Bash
adds Write and Glob

decisions.rationale: Edits stay on Scope files; Bash runs the tier command through hpy and read-only git.

decisions.question: The writing-docstrings SkillSpec is frozen (mode new): a frozen spec takes only part changes, greens and --refreeze, its behaviors stay locked, and its B5 contract pins and session-role B6-B8 scenarios no longer fit the change. How does the strap gate cover this edit?

options.summary: git mv the frozen spec folder to docs/plans/strap/_archive/writing-docstrings-187/, then strap.py new writing-docstrings --edit opens a fresh edit spec
keep the frozen spec: add_part the agent and driver, greens on the new hash, freeze --refreeze; no new behaviors
skip the strap gate; the plan's tests and the contract test are the proof

decisions.rationale: Developer decision: a fresh edit spec lets the new dispatch and -in behaviors take baselines and moves B6-B8 to the docstring-writer role; the frozen spec stays readable in the archive.

decisions.question: How does resolve_scope tell a path from a bare symbol, and what happens to a file reached twice?

options.summary: a token is a path when it holds '::', '/' or '\', ends in '.py', or names an existing file or directory; a separator-free token that names a directory and also a function in a named file is a problem (write '<dir>/'); scopes key on the resolved path: a file reached twice bare is one 'all' scope, '::' names of one file merge in first-seen order, a file both whole (bare or through a directory) and narrowed is a problem; scopes sort by path
spec D1 as written: a path is a token naming an existing .py file or directory

decisions.rationale: Review EXECUTABILITY-2, DESIGN-2, TESTS-1, DESIGN-3: existence alone turns a missing path into a symbol and a folder-named symbol into a scope; without a dedup rule -p can put two agents on one file (spec anti-goal).

decisions.question: Where do probes go, and how is a probe left by an interrupted run removed?

options.summary: one probe per distinct parent folder of the rows, listed on one probe row; each written path is appended to <state_dir>/writing-docstrings/probes.txt; every driver run and --clear-probe (no path) remove the recorded probes that sit under the project, carry PROBE_NAME and are untracked, then drop the record; a git-tracked file of that name is never overwritten
spec D5 as written: one probe beside the first target, cleared by path

decisions.rationale: Review DESIGN-6, DESIGN-7, TESTS-3, TESTS-7: one folder's probe does not cover Edit rules elsewhere, and a probe from a crashed run was cleaned only by chance. Refines D5; the probe still sits beside the real targets.

decisions.question: Which checkout anchors the driver?

options.summary: --repo, else the git top level of the first path token's folder (resolved against cwd), else cwd; a token outside that root is a problem
--repo or cwd

decisions.rationale: Review DESIGN-10: docstring_tiers.py anchored at the file, so a file in a d-w worktree worked from the main session; cwd anchoring would refuse it.

decisions.question: What does the session do when it writes new functions itself, or is asked which layout to use?

options.summary: functions the session itself wrote count as an explicit ask: it dispatches with -in scoped to them (file.py::name); a layout question is answered from docstring_format.md without a dispatch; the description keeps 'writing'
drop the 'writing' and 'choosing a layout' triggers

decisions.rationale: Review DESIGN-1: with every tier rule in the agent file, the authoring trigger would otherwise leave new code undocumented or written without the convention.

decisions.question: Which judgment behaviors does the fresh edit spec baseline, and how do B6-B8 survive?

options.summary: baseline only moves the base skill does not make: (J1) the session dispatches every printed row and never edits a docstring itself; (J2) the session passes -in only on an explicit ask or for functions it wrote (D14), and turns a plain request's non-argument instructions into the Developer guidance line; (J3) the docstring-writer edits only its Scope files when the guidance tempts a wider tidy-up; (J4) on a Probe: yes row the agent reports 'Probe tier: SUCCESS|BLOCKED' and 'Probe edit: SUCCESS|BLOCKED' and skips the D8 sections. B6-B8 are unchanged rules carried by moved prose, pinned by the contract test on the agent file, not re-baselined
baseline B6-B8 on the docstring-writer role

decisions.rationale: Review RULES-2, DESIGN-4, DESIGN-5: edit-spec baselines carry the base SKILL.md, which already teaches B6-B8, so their baselines pass and strap-skills would drop them.
